summary: The structural experiment is well annotated, but result invalidation/redraw and worker-opening ownership prevent trustworthy interactive reruns.

lenses.smells_idioms: Read the full control/preview/mesh/queue/result pipeline. No raw properties or redundant box aliases. frames returns as the final value and owns the adopted session with finally; opening-future ownership and result publication need repair (findings). KratosSession.kt solveAsync/cancel/openMeshAsync were read for revision and cancellation contracts.
lenses.imports: Imports include a Kratos star and explicit mesh/native/AtomicReference APIs. No deterministic import-analyzer report was available in the assignment tree; defer removals to coordinator analysis and retain the star without resolution evidence.
lenses.whitespace: Control rows are readable as one slider per line; queue branches use semicolons, but a bulk formatter must preserve the control table and status-string structure. No whitespace-only finding.
lenses.comments: Units, optional installation, fixed/load regions, quadratic element purpose and display-only exaggeration are explained at the decision points. The redraw comment currently promises more than its membership-only stamp implements.
lenses.glsl: No GLSL body or embedded shader string.
lenses.live_coding: No authored fragment markers or declaration/reset pairs exist. Sliders intentionally update an AtomicReference; preserve that thread boundary. Async request snapshots and repeat Solve need verification before claiming rerunnable behavior.
lenses.helpers: Checked Already in Field, Approved and Declined. Existing KratosSession.cancel and revision-bearing results provide the necessary primitives; no generic helper is needed to fix the local state machine. Do not replace numeric diagnostics with the approved x.f3 idea blindly: this formatter accepts Any? and selectable precision.

findings.issue: Replacing a finished result for the same nodesPerCell leaves this stamp unchanged. After the initial comparison, Solve can complete for a new load without redrawing meshes or replacing the Solving status; the redraw only resumes if exaggeration changes. The API returns distinct SimulationResult objects with revisions, but this stamp sees only map membership.
findings.proposed_change: Track a publication counter or actual result identities/revisions in the draw stamp and advance it on every accepted result; reset it when the comparison is invalidated.
findings.verification: Replay initial comparison, change tip load and Solve the same order without changing exaggeration; require updated displacement, mesh and terminal status, then repeat unchanged inputs.

findings.issue: The pending future has no immutable input key. Changing arm/element size clears results at lines 128-129, but a future for the previous shape can later insert its answer into that cleared map; queued comparison orders read the then-current settings separately. Load is absent from the comparison key, so the Same load comparison can combine answers computed under different loads.
findings.proposed_change: Queue immutable requests containing arm, mesh size, load and order; retain the submitted key with each future/result and reject stale geometry/load publications. Make both Compare orders requests share one snapshot and clear/label old output on invalidation.
findings.verification: Change arm during a pending solve and load between compare orders; confirm old futures never relabel or mix with current answers and both compared orders have the same load.

findings.issue: The opening future is local to the meshing branch. Stopping/rerunning while frame() waits reaches finally with session still null; the asynchronous open can then finish and create an unowned worker. KratosSession.openMeshAsync closes a newly created session when opening.complete(session) fails, so cancelling the future provides an existing cleanup path.
findings.proposed_change: Keep the opening future under the same try/finally ownership as session, cancel it on stop/rerun, and close an already completed unadopted session across the completion/cancellation race.
findings.verification: Stop and rerun while a delayed worker opens; observe that every created worker/session is closed and no old status/result publishes into the new run.

verification_needed: Compile/replay this transcript with optional Kratos, TetGen and Manifold available. Exercise initial comparison, same-order repeated Solve, input changes during solving, and stop/rerun during opening; capture current result meshes/status and check worker shutdown.

summary: Keep the source: all four bodies use explicit geometry experiments, scoped native ownership and well placed mathematical commentary. A slice visitor is an optional API consolidation, not a required rewrite.

lenses.smells_idioms: Read all four bodies: the macro capture comment, degenerate-cut experiment, volume-normalized raw/canonical comparison with CPU raster output, and Ceres/convergence/fill-rule experiment. Solid.scope wraps every solid-building path; each slice uses use and extracts JVM values before closing. Solid.kt confirms scopes close intermediates and Unit avoids returning/retaining native values. No raw properties, graph lookups or lifecycle registrations.
lenses.imports: Explicit Solid/toSolid/FillRule/PngEncoder imports match the visible API calls. A deterministic import report was not supplied; retain all until coordinator analyzer classifies intro coverage. No speculative import removal.
lenses.whitespace: Keep authored table header/value rows aligned as semantic rows, along with case labels and explicit three-component vector arithmetic. Folded helpers separate setup from the short comparisons; nested contour loops have clear panel/layer/ring roles.
lenses.comments: Comments justify midpoint cuts, volume normalization, shared scale, index preservation, welding, signed-volume rejection and the fill-rule comparison. Nine-decimal formatting is explicitly necessary for near-face cuts; preserve that precision.
lenses.glsl: No GLSL. The IntArray/PngEncoder routine is an actual CPU raster of computed slices rather than a replacement GPU capture; the separate first body invokes a retained linux-nvidia macro capture.
lenses.live_coding: Preserve all :::static and :::fold directives. No //%- fragment markers or declaration/reset pairs. LAYERS/PANEL and SWEEP are visible controls; the first body is deliberately only a macro driver, not a standalone geometry program.
lenses.helpers: Checked helper register and geometry sources. Existing Solid.scope/use solve ownership. A midpoint slice sampling helper could consolidate four traversals, but is an optional new API proposal; the teaching math and concrete boundary-cut cases should remain explicit. Authored table rows already match the open formatter convention.

helper_proposals.title: Visit midpoint slices with scoped native ownership
helper_proposals.rationale: cutHeights, areasOf, contoursOf, riemann and overlap repeat midpoint-height computation and Section.use. A small optional visitor could remove nested generic scaffolding and centralize native lifetime without hiding how the Riemann sum is formed.
helper_proposals.before: cutHeights(s, n).map { z -> s.slice(z).use { it.area } }; a separate traversal repeats slicing for toPolygons()
helper_proposals.after: Proposed API sketch only: s.sampleSlices(n) { z, section -> section.area to section.toPolygons() }; callers still compute sum * height / n explicitly.
helper_proposals.existing_or_declined_check: Read BOX_CODE_HELPER_IDEAS.md Already in Field/Approved/Declined/Open. Searched geometry sources for layer/stack/cutHeights/sliceHeights helpers: Solid.slice and Solid.scope exist, but no midpoint-sampling visitor was found. No declined dispatch-sizing or implicit geometry proposal is revived.
helper_proposals.verification: If approved, compare sample z, area, contour winding/count and fill-rule results against the current explicit loops, verify Section closure on exceptions, and recapture the three CPU boxes. A callback must not return a closed Section as a usable native value.

summary: Keep the educational reduction/physics structure, but freeze the actual landed geometry, verify it rather than only target coordinates, refresh stale runtime comments, and expose the advertised tempo controls.

lenses.smells_idioms: Read the complete one-body program: source terms/orders, WL labels and BFS pose, per-cell reduction/physics/landing, FLine geometry, viewer loop and oracle report. No renderer is needed by the Three.js output API; no raw property access or box alias exists. Box.three returns stable viewer state and streams updates under a box/name id. Target/display state separation has a concrete defect.
lenses.imports: The single explicit FLine import is used but may be intro-redundant; no analyzer report exists in the packet, so no removal is proposed pending coordinator deterministic evidence.
lenses.whitespace: The term/scheduler/palette rows are authored tables and should survive formatting. Multi-variable semicolon arithmetic in the force calculation is dense; splitting it mechanically is lower priority than preserving the XYZ force groups and repairing landing.
lenses.comments: Topology, port order, newborn positions, physics and transparent framing cage have useful intent comments. Historical driver/panel diagnosis requires current verification; description handoff is identified in the finding. Three-round WL is a refinement heuristic, not a proof of canonical graph labeling: tied sorted labels preserve Net.nodes creation order, which interactionnets.kt documents explicitly.
lenses.glsl: No shader source. FLine is sent to the browser viewer; the no-renderer requirement is consistent with Box.three.
lenses.live_coding: No //%- markers or declaration/reset pairs. The driver is a blocking bounded sleep loop. Tempo/cap/landing literals should be exposed as controls, and any migration to frames must first prove renderer-free tick/stop behavior and preserve oracle output. Actual rendered state must be verified, not only target coordinates.
lenses.helpers: Read existing/approved/declined helper lists. FLine endpoints are already expressed directly with moveTo/lineTo; data/breakNext/rect/circle offer no improvement. No new general canonical-layout helper is proposed from one specialized example; the WL tie/creation-order caveat should be investigated with node-order permutations before any shared API claim.

findings.issue: physics continues after done and after landing reaches 40. land then stops applying corrections, so early-finished rows move away from the target while later rows reduce; the last landing interpolation also only applies a 0.35 fraction rather than snapping. The printed identical-pose verdict at line 335 compares c.pose target coordinates, not the pos used by geometry(), so it cannot detect the visible drift.
findings.proposed_change: Stop physics when entering the landing phase or freeze the final pose at its last step; snap to target and clear velocity. Compute a separate verification of displayed positions and topology under the node correspondence rather than using target coordinate multisets as evidence of identical rendering.
findings.verification: Run all five rows through completion, record displayed pos immediately after landing and many later ticks while other rows run, and require no drift plus equivalent relative edge geometry. Inspect final viewer and compare actual positions to targets.
